## Acceptance criteria

REQ-01–03 are met. The catalog is exposed through [`CommandSchema::generate`](crates/jit/src/schema.rs:243), rendered to [`events.md`](docs/reference/events.md:1), and guarded against stale serde tags and `issue_id` associations in [`event_catalog` tests](crates/jit/src/domain/event_catalog.rs:765).

## Architecture and separation of concerns

The catalog is pure domain logic in [`event_catalog.rs`](crates/jit/src/domain/event_catalog.rs:575); storage serialization remains behind [`IssueStore::append_event`](crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:737).

## Functional paradigm

The implementation uses iterator pipelines for catalog and documentation projection.

## Correctness and invariants

The exact five-tag no-issue set is asserted in [`test_no_issue_set_is_exactly_the_shared_state_events`](crates/jit/src/domain/event_catalog.rs:853). Serialization and `get_issue_id` agreement are both verified.

## Safety

No unsafe code or PID-related changes were introduced.

## Testing

The current-commit `cargo-ci` evidence passed: fmt, Clippy, and 3,659 tests. Per instruction, I did not rerun tests. `./scripts/jit-validate.sh` passed.

## Error handling

No swallowed serialization errors remain in the production catalog path.

## CLI contract

`jit --schema` now carries the machine-consumable `events` array.

## Documentation

The generated reference is linked from storage, CLI, and index documentation. New public catalog APIs include examples.

## Prior review feedback

All three prior findings are resolved by the current commit.

## JIT issue management

The prerequisite dependency is done; no unmet dependencies remain.
